clue.text: Second mate welcoming Republican like Bush

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so the husband word holds the party letter

parts.note: a hubby is a husband, an informal word for a marriage mate

explanation.surface: A political second-in-command takes in a Republican who resembles George Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the US president, but it is the plant; the capital is only there for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrubby describes something resembling a shrub, and a bush is a shrub.

clue.text: Yo-yo with ace spots turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: A is ace on playing cards
to spot is to see, so spots means sees

explanation.surface: A yo-yo with a fine pattern of spots appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: Yo-yo is used as a verb: to swing back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to oscillate up and down, much as a yo-yo moves.

clue.text: Spoil losing weight, getting evenly round figure

indicators.note: getting means the next piece is added on
losing means the weight letter drops out

parts.note: to wreck something is to spoil it

indicators.note: evenly means taking the even-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A diet story: losing weight spoilt someone's round figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure is a verb here, not a body shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to calculate or suppose, just as to reckon is.

clue.text: Theban plays fail to make peaceful appeal

indicators.note: plays means the letters are toyed with and rearranged

parts.note: to bomb is to fail badly, especially of a show

explanation.surface: Greek plays from Thebes fail to put across a pacifist message.
explanation.definitionFit: Ban the Bomb was the slogan of the nuclear disarmament campaign, a plea for peace.

clue.text: Somewhat rowdy, a hoodlum?

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A question whether a rather noisy thug counts as a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a rude, coarse lout, from the brutish creatures in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Place Franco-German articles in sack

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for Place in street addresses
UN is a French article and DER a German one

explanation.surface: Someone puts French and German articles into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, looting it by force.

clue.text: Small amount of cash turned up (100 pounds) outside diner

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: 1P, one penny, is a tiny sum
C is the Roman numeral for 100
nicker is British slang for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A tiny sum appeared, plus a hundred pounds, outside a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like a container signal, but 'outside diner' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnicker eats in the open air, so is a diner out of doors.

clue.text: Cricket scores you heard upped for Ashes holders

indicators.note: upped means raised, so in a down clue the U letter moves up the word

parts.note: runs are the scores in cricket
U sounds like you when said

explanation.surface: A cricket report: scores raised for the side holding the Ashes trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series, fought over a tiny urn, but here the ashes are cremation remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vessels used to keep the ashes of the dead.

clue.text: Wilde, say, could be a poet

indicators.note: could be means the letters might be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde, for example, might count as a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Day-Lewis was a British poet, Poet Laureate from 1968.

clue.text: River weeds in new ports, perhaps

indicators.note: new means the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: River weeds growing in new harbours.
explanation.walkthrough: Ports look like harbours; they are fortified wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a fortified wine, usually red, so ports are examples of red wines.

clue.text: One's rehabilitated a defector to Labour?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a former prisoner, someone released and reformed
second meaning: read as ..., a former Conservative who has switched to the Labour party

explanation.walkthrough: CON is the usual short form for Conservative, so a former Tory is cheekily an ex-con.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-convict is someone who has served a prison sentence and been released into society.

clue.text: Stock cut, investing currency from the east

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the cut word wraps the currency

parts.note: hacked means cut roughly

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading right to left, so the currency is backwards

parts.note: the yen is the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A financial tale: stock is cut while money from the Far East is invested.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock and investing suggest the markets, but stock here is an adjective meaning trite.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase is a hackneyed one: overused and unoriginal.

clue.text: A rejected work proposition includes nothing for great model

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the work abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: includes means the proposition word holds the zero inside

parts.note: a thesis is a proposition put forward for argument
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An academic proposal is turned down even though it contains nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An apotheosis is the perfect example or highest form of something, an ideal paragon.

clue.text: Setter was in the van, needing return fare from here

indicators.note: return means coming back, so the setter-plus-led letters are read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I
to be in the van (vanguard) is to be at the front, so led

explanation.surface: The setter drove the van and now needs the fare to get back.
explanation.walkthrough: Van suggests a vehicle and fare a ticket price; 'in the van' really means leading, and fare is food.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods, so fare comes from there.

clue.text: Extremely coquettish kind of yellow jumper turned up where one goes at night

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: amber is a yellowish-orange colour

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a top is a garment; jumper is British for a sweater

explanation.surface: A flirtatious yellow sweater was found where someone sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber pot is a bedroom vessel used as a toilet during the night.

clue.text: How to make techie get conversation going

indicators.note: how to make asks for the instruction that would produce the following word, so the answer itself is read as wordplay

parts.note: breaking (rearranging) the letters of THE ICE gives this word

explanation.surface: Advice on how to turn someone into a computer enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'break' is an anagram signal working on 'the ice', whose letters give TECHIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To break the ice is the idiom for easing initial awkwardness so people start chatting.

clue.text: Rendezvous in French bar

parts.note: en is French for in
a counter is a bar in a pub or shop

explanation.surface: A meeting arranged in a French bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a meeting, as is a rendezvous.

clue.text: American who drew game, with both sides full of energy

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: full of means the sides hold the energy letter between them

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, both sides
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A US sportsman drew a game, both teams playing with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drew' suggests a tied match; it means made drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was an American painter and etcher.

clue.text: Whizz over finale of Bach, needing one piece for bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a whizz is an expert, a pro

indicators.note: the finale is the last letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A musical prodigy plays the end of a Bach piece, needing one more bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a measure of music; here it is the verb meaning forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to forbid or ban it.

clue.text: Murmur about a strange blemish or rash

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the murmur word goes round the rest

parts.note: a hum is a low murmur
rum is British slang for odd or strange
a scar is a mark or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A doctor mutters about an odd skin mark or rash.
explanation.walkthrough: Blemish and rash look like skin trouble; rash is in fact the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Harum-scarum means reckless and impetuous, just as a rash person acts without thinking.

clue.text: Parnassian location's key character there

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a keyboard
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character used there in Greece

explanation.surface: Mount Parnassus's key figure is found nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Greece, where Parnassus stands, so the character is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi, home of Apollo's oracle, lies on the slopes of Mount Parnassus in Greece.

clue.text: University in Irish district wanting new hall

indicators.note: in means the university letter is placed inside
wanting means lacking, so the new letter is dropped

parts.note: Antrim is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A university in an Irish district lacks a new hall.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a central open hall or court in a building.

clue.text: Like that hotel round Westminster area

parts.note: so means in that way, like that
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone describes a hotel near Westminster.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of London lying within the City of Westminster, known for nightlife.

clue.text: Extra time to follow chaps who do yoga?

indicators.note: to follow means the time letter comes after the chaps

parts.note: yoga practitioners are bendy, so supple men

explanation.surface: Extra time is needed for the men at the yoga class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra time' looks like a football phrase, but Extra stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement is something added as an extra, an addition to complete or enhance.

clue.text: What you get from sweet food and extremes of gluttony?

definitions.text: What you get from sweet food and extremes of gluttony?

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a dessert

indicators.note: extremes means the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Eating puddings and overeating makes you plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudgy means podgy, short and plump, which is what overindulgence leaves you.

clue.text: Exam not fine for a learner

indicators.note: not means the fine letter is taken away

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: An exam result that isn't good enough for a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a learner' seems to be part of the surface, but it supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

clue.text: Made free carpet kept in cover

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the scolding word sits within the cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover
to carpet someone is British slang for to scold them, to berate

explanation.surface: Free carpet was kept under a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpet is a verb: to carpet someone, in British usage, is to give them a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated means set free, released from captivity or constraint.

clue.text: Knocked back one's ginger drink

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed; here the words go backwards

parts.note: I is one, and 's adds S
ginger as energy or liveliness means pep

explanation.surface: Someone downed their ginger drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger looks like ginger ale or beer, but it means pep, as in to ginger up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepsi is a brand of cola, a soft drink.

clue.text: Venomous sort of chatterbox losing face

indicators.note: losing face means dropping the first letter, the front of the word

parts.note: a prattler is someone who chatters on

explanation.surface: A spiteful gossip suffers embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: Venomous suggests a nasty person; it is literal: a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattler is a rattlesnake, a poisonous American snake.

clue.text: Rare element of maturity adult leaves out

indicators.note: leaves means the adult letter departs from the fodder
out signals the remaining letters are disordered, put out of place

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Something rare about grown-up maturity that adults abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttrium is a rare-earth metal, one of the chemical elements, named after Ytterby in Sweden.
